Hideko was interested to see if there was a relationship between what people earn and the age which they left education or training. She says her data supports the conclusion that more education causes people to earn a lower hourly rate of pay. Give one reason why Hideko’s conclusion might not be valid.
“Respondents who left education later would have significantly less work experience than those who left education earlier. This could be the cause of the reduced income shown in her results.”
3. Eight students estimated the mass of a bag of sweets, in grams. First they estimated without touching the bag. They then picked it up and estimated the mass again.
(a) Draw a scatter diagram to represent the data.
(b) Describe and interpret the correlation between the two variables.
Positive correlation. A student who guessed above (or below) the mean in one test tended to do the same in the other.

(a) Draw a scatter diagram to represent the data.
(c) Donal says a slow connection reduces the value of a house. Give one reason why this conclusion may be invalid.

(b) Use your knowledge of the large data set to explain whether there is likely to be a causal relationship.

(d) State two ways to make better use of the large data set to model the relationship.
For each percentage-point increase in humidity, predicted mean visibility falls by 106 decametres.
High humidity (above 95%) can cause mist and fog, reducing visibility. A causal link is plausible.
